notes.text: The page continues a preceding discussion with an underlined isomorphisme and states that (2) is obtained by passage to the profinite. It inserts hom de before suites exactes and displays a two-row diagram labelled (4) at the left. The upper-left exception note lists g=0, nu=0,1,2 and circles only g=1,nu=0, followed by the author's question mark.

The diagram's first, second and last upper links are bare shafts; the middle map to Gamma and the other main map heads are pointed. Gamma curves down/right to the clipped Out term. The paired vertical label is rendered as the two wavy strokes actually visible, consistent with scan026; its mathematical intention is not separately settled. Its cancelled right label, the last vertical tip and the clipped continuation after Out remain local doubts. A source X basepoint is present in the lower middle object even though both witnesses omitted it.

The crowded line below the diagram appears to begin admettons. The short graph after completed T is retained as arrow / severely reduced est, and the lower word as invariant / injective. Neither reader can locate an independent second est before that lower word. The operator argument contains the author’s literal question mark. This local treatment preserves the unclear wording without supplying grammatical completion.

The first diagonal note is headed Version corrigée éventuelle and gives a normalizer formulation with additional automorphism, symmetric-group and local-structure conditions. The word locale has quotation marks plus a three-sided angular frame; a separate divider passes beneath the note near the final T indices. The frame and divider are not treated as cancellations. Crowded closing signs and autom remain uncertain.

The main paragraph asks that the arrow (1), described as the central vertical arrow of (5), be an iso. The source references (1) and (5) are retained although the displayed diagram is numbered (4). The consequence is called a caractérisation of Gamma. In the quotient, the underbrace begins around the low 1/following opening parenthesis and ends under the completed inner argument; it does not cover Autextlac or the denominator.

The second diagonal note lists exceptional (g,nu) and refers to pi_1 of an X with a genuine low Q-like index, followed by a partially reduced abelian-group phrase. A separate rectangle and zigzag cancel several lines; only their surviving fragments are transcribed, with physically illegible spans. The lower diagonal note cautions about g=0,nu=3 and adds commutation conditions with exterior operations of S_3.

The example retains the source spelling celà. Its final Autextlac expression has two opening round parentheses and only one closing parenthesis before the period; this incomplete punctuation is preserved. The lower diagram similarly lacks a separately visible closing set brace. These observations are source-graph decisions, not mathematical corrections.

Pencil footer 29 is included with unknown hand attribution. The ordinary/bold/blackboard rendering of Q or P is not treated as a new symbol. All physical lower indices, superscripts, bars, wedges and circle marks were inspected individually.

Limited group-theoretic check relevant to the normalizer revision: for any subgroup T of a group A, each t in T normalizes T, so T is contained in N_A(T); by the defining equality nTn^{-1}=T for n in N_A(T), T is normal there, and N_A(T)/T is a group. By contrast A/T needs normality of T in A. This checks the elementary role of a normalizer in the marginal revision; it proves neither the source’s proposed identification with Gamma nor normality in the full exterior-automorphism group. It does not settle the written arrow/est or invariant/injective ambiguity.
